audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is called a knockup in three places: 'Open with Facebreaker to knock you up before you reach three stacks' (wants.foe[0]), 'He can Facebreaker to knock you up before the third An Acquired Taste stack lands' (mid), and 'Sett's Facebreaker knock-up can interrupt your An Acquired Taste stacking' (whys[3]).
audit.why: Facebreaker pulls enemies inward and stuns or slows them. There is no displacement upward anywhere in it. This matters beyond pedantry because knockups and stuns behave differently against everything a top laner cares about — tenacity applies to one and not the other — and a player who believes he ate a knockup will draw the wrong conclusion about why his combo broke.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker is a pull into a stun, not a knockup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker's stun condition is absent from the entire entry.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit: Facebreaker pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of Sett and stuns them, and 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a 1v1 that is a positioning rule with a hard mechanical payoff — Sett has to get himself between Tahm Kench and something else, usually the minion wave, to earn the stun. Stand so that you and the wave are on the same side of him and the ability degrades to a slow, which a tank with grey health simply walks through. This is the single highest-leverage piece of tech in the matchup and it appears nowhere, in either layer, across a 1175-game sample.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker only stuns if Sett has enemies on both sides of him. Keep yourself and the wave on the same side of him and it is a slow, not a stun — never let him step between you and your minions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Knuckle Down scales with the target's maximum health, while the entry's entire itemization plan is Heartsteel.
audit.why: Knuckle Down makes Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage based off the target's max health. Tahm Kench's core build is a stacking-health item and his passive already converts health into damage, so every Heartsteel stack he takes makes Sett's basic trade pattern hit him harder. That does not make Heartsteel wrong — grey health scales with it too — but a player choosing between Heartsteel and a resistance item deserves to know the trade is not free, and the entry currently presents the item spike as pure upside three separate times.
audit.corrected: Knuckle Down scales off your max health, so every Heartsteel stack feeds his short trades. The answer is armour alongside the HP, not more HP.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields claim Devour wipes Sett's Grit: 'stun into Devour removes Sett from the fight and erases his entire grit bar' (spikes[0]) and 'Swallowing Sett resets his entire Haymaker grit bar to zero — he comes out with nothing to show for the trade' (early).
audit.why: Nothing in either kit supports Devour clearing Grit, and needsResearch on the Tahm Kench kit is empty by design, meaning unknown rather than confirmed. Grit is stored damage that decays on its own timer; a two-second swallow is not obviously long enough to empty it. I have not replaced this with an opposite claim, because I cannot verify that either — I have rewritten the sentences around the part that is verifiable, which is that Grit comes from damage he has already taken.
audit.corrected: Do not promise a Grit reset. What is certain is that Grit is charged by the damage you deal him before he casts, so poking him into a full bar hands him a bigger shield and a bigger punch.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sett's ultimate is written as 'Showstopper' in spikes[1], wants.foe[2], mid, late and whys[4].
audit.why: The ability is The Show Stopper. Minor next to the Facebreaker error, but it is the same class of defect the calibration examples call out.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names Haymaker as the tracked cooldown with no number, and the content layer says to commit when 'his E is on cooldown' with no number either.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and Facebreaker is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10. Facebreaker is the one that decides whether your 3-stack commit survives contact, and at rank 1 that is a 16-second window — long enough to be a real plan rather than a vibe.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker is 16s at rank 1; that is the window your stun-into-Devour lives in. Haymaker is 18s and is a damage problem, not a commit problem.

edits.before: Your An Acquired Taste stun is fully online — land Tongue Lash twice in a short trade, then walk into melee range for the third stack: stun into Devour removes Sett from the fight and erases his entire grit bar.
edits.after: Your An Acquired Taste stun is fully online — land Tongue Lash twice in a short trade, then step in for the third stack. Keep the wave on your own side of Sett so Facebreaker can only slow you, never stun.

edits.before: Open with Facebreaker to knock you up before you reach three stacks, resetting your An Acquired Taste counter and winning the trade for free
edits.after: Step between you and your minions so Facebreaker has a target on each side and stuns instead of slowing, then punish before you reach three stacks

edits.before: Build grit with his passive double-punch in prolonged brawls and detonate Haymaker for true damage before you can activate Thick Skin
edits.after: Soak your poke to charge Grit, then detonate Haymaker — the shield and the centre true damage both scale with the damage you dealt him

edits.before: Stack An Acquired Taste in short brush trades — auto, Tongue Lash slow, auto — so the stun is ready before Sett can build his Haymaker grit bar
edits.after: Never let Sett stand between you and your wave — with enemies on one side only, Facebreaker slows instead of stunning and your 3-stack commit survives

edits.before: Fish for the three-stack stun in lane and deny Sett the sustained brawl his passive double-punch wants — short burst trades only
edits.after: Buy armour alongside the health — Knuckle Down scales off your max HP, so raw Heartsteel stacking feeds his two empowered punches

edits.before: Sett's Facebreaker knock-up can interrupt your An Acquired Taste stacking before the stun lands — do not commit unless his E is on cooldown or you already have two stacks banked.
edits.after: Facebreaker pulls and stuns only with enemies on both sides of him — deny it by keeping the wave on your own side, or wait out its full 16 seconds before you commit.

edits.before: Heartsteel and Sunfire mean every extended trade now drains Sett faster than his grit restores his health — force long attrition fights he cannot win and heal the Haymaker damage out of combat.
edits.after: Heartsteel and Sunfire win you the attrition, but Knuckle Down reads your max health — pair the HP with armour or his two empowered punches scale up alongside your item spike.

edits.before: At level 1 Tongue Lash range keeps you safe: slow Sett when he steps up and deny him the clean passive double-punch reset he needs to win short trades. Do not walk into his fist range just to land the slow — that hands him the first strike and starts filling his grit bar before yours is full. At level 3 the dynamic shifts completely in your favour: fish for two early stacks with a Tongue Lash and a quick auto, then let him swing thinking the trade is going his way before you drop the stun and Devour him. Swallowing Sett resets his entire Haymaker grit bar to zero — he comes out with nothing to show for the trade.
edits.after: At level 1 Tongue Lash range keeps you safe: slow Sett when he steps up and deny him the clean passive double-punch reset he needs to win short trades. Do not walk into fist range just to land the slow — that hands him the first strike, and every point of damage you take is Grit charging his Haymaker shield and its true-damage centre. At level 3 the dynamic shifts your way: fish two stacks with a Tongue Lash and an auto, keep the wave on your own side of him so Facebreaker cannot find a target on both sides of him, then stun and Devour him when he swings back.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Sett's best window before you have your ultimate. He can Facebreaker to knock you up before the third An Acquired Taste stack lands, breaking your stun setup and winning the extended brawl with his passive double-punch chip damage. Respect it: do not commit to a full combo unless you have two stacks already banked and his E is on cooldown. At level 6 you gain Abyssal Voyage, but be cautious — Sett's Showstopper is equally threatening, and if he suppresses you while your Thick Skin bar is loaded with grey health, the true-damage slam converts your built-up healing into his kill pressure. Time your E activation before the slam lands, not after.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Sett's best window before you have your ultimate. Facebreaker pulls you in and stuns — but only when he has enemies on both sides of him, so the whole phase is a positioning fight over whether he gets between you and your wave. Deny that and it is a slow on 16 seconds you can walk straight through. Haymaker is 18 seconds, and the Grit filling it is the damage you just dealt him, so chipping a low Sett only makes his punch bigger. At level 6 you gain Devour, but respect The Show Stopper: if he carries you off while your Thick Skin bar is loaded, the slam cashes in grey health you never converted. Press E before the slam lands, not after.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. W-dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, and it only stuns with enemies on both sides of him. Keep the wave on your side and it is a slow. - Haymaker 18s: Grit is your own damage back.

edits.before: Sett wins by landing Haymaker, denying your pattern, and out-trading your engage windows.
edits.after: Sett wins by getting between you and the wave for a Facebreaker stun, then Haymaker.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The positioning window: never let Sett stand between you and your wave, or Facebreaker upgrades from a slow to a stun.

notes: Largest sample in my slice at 1175 games, and the entry was missing the one rule that decides the lane: Facebreaker stuns only when Sett has enemies on both sides of him, otherwise it slows. Against a melee tank that is a pure positioning problem with a clean answer, and it was absent from both layers while the ability was simultaneously mislabelled as a knockup in three fields. I did not assert that Devour fails to clear Sett's Grit — I only removed the unsupported claim that it does, and rewrote around the part that is verifiable from Riot's text (Grit is charged by damage he has taken).
